items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: Dissolving is a physical process rather than a chemical reaction. When some salts dissolve in water heat is given out (exothermic), but when others dissolve the process is endothermic.

items.label: text
items.text: Safety Note: Wear eye protection and avoid skin contact with the acid and alkali. Safety Note: Wear eye protection and avoid skin contact with the acid and alkali.

items.label: text
items.text: Note: the temperature of the water decreases, so the reaction is endothermic and heat is absorbed from the surroundings for the dissolving process to occur.

items.label: text
items.text: We can use this data to calculate the molar enthalpy change for dissolving ammonium chloride.

items.label: text
items.text: Heat absorbed: Q = mc∆T = 100 × 4.18 × (18.3 - 15.1) = 1337.6J = 1.3376kJ Here we assume the following:

items.label: list_item
items.text: The specific heat capacity of the diluted solution of ammonium chloride is the same as that of water. This is quite a reasonable assumption because the mixture is mostly water.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The mass of the solution is 100 g. The mass of the ammonium chloride is relatively small and it is ignored in the calculation. There are other major sources of error in the experiment, for example heat absorbed from the surrounding air, which makes much more difference to the results.

items.label: text
items.text: Now we need to calculate how much heat is absorbed when 1 mole of ammonium chloride dissolves in excess water.

items.label: text
items.text: The relative formula mass of ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) is 14 + 4 × 1 + 35.5 = 53.5.

items.label: text
items.text: Number of moles (n) of ammonium chloride dissolved

items.label: text
items.text: The amount of heat absorbed when dissolving 1 mole of ammonium chloride in water is therefore:

items.label: formula
items.text: N H _ { 4 } C I ( s ) \to N H _ { 4 } C I ( a q ) \quad \Delta H = + 1 3 . 8 k J / m o l

items.label: text
items.text: The positive sign shows that heat is absorbed and the dissolving of ammonium chloride in water is an endothermic process (the temperature goes down).
